content.thinking:
I'm drafting the postmortem's symptom section: account pages failed for many shoppers, backed by the account-page request failures and error rate. I'm now starting the causal chain, with the first item being the symptom itself.

I'm working through the causal chain for the postmortem, now at the step where the ZeroDivisionError in the spend summary code is tied to the monthly-spend feature flag being switched on, and checking which other possible causes such as deploys and other flag changes are ruled out.

I'm checking the remaining candidate causes, deploys and other flag changes, and finding that nothing else in the record accounts for the onset. Next I'm working out why flipping the flag breaks the page: the account figure is computed as the month's total divided by the number of purchases this month, and for shoppers with no purchases that count is zero, which raises the ZeroDivisionError.

I'm settling on the root cause: with the monthly-spend feature on, the account page divides the month's total by how many purchases the shopper made this month, and a shopper with none makes that count zero, which triggers the ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py. I'm also noting that the spend-per-item figure here rests on a reading of the code I haven't actually run.

I'm weighing how to present the contributing factors: the flag change went to all traffic at once with no check seen gating it for a share first, and I'm considering a proposal to roll out flag changes to a small slice of traffic before going wide.

I'm checking the second contributing factor: no test seemed to cover the flag-on path for a shopper with no purchases this month, so the new tests would fail against the current code. The existing tests only exercise the flag-off path. I'm considering a proposed item to require tests that exercise the flag-on path before any flag can be enabled in production.

I'm weighing whether the average-spend calculation should keep raising for shoppers with no purchases at all, since the existing tests now expect that error. I'll propose a decision item on that, to either keep the error on purpose or handle it.

I'm now checking the remaining contributing factors and the still-at-risk note, then the lessons section, where I'm looking at how the Investigator Agent placed the onset at the flag-change minute and tied it to the P1 change.

I'm filling in the lessons section now: the Investigator Agent placed the onset at the minute of the flag change and tied it to the P1, the Mitigation Agent reverted the flag and then confirmed the recovery, and the Code-Fix Agent proposed a draft fix in PR #527.

I'm settling on the assumptions section: the mechanism depends on Code-Fix's reading of spend_summary.py, and I still have to note that the source it read may not match the revision the replicas were running, since the deployment history doesn't name the revision.

I'm splitting the staged-rollout idea into two separate action items: one to prevent flag switch-ons from reaching all traffic at once, and one to automatically revert a flag when the error rate rises during its rollout.

I'm adding the process item that requires tests for the flag-on path before any flag goes live. I'm also planning a separate prevent item to review whether the flag-off average should still raise for accounts with no purchases at all. Next I'm dating the causal chain: the P1 starts at its recorded time, the flag goes on at 02:02, and the ZeroDivisionError begins that same minute.

I'm laying out the causal chain's later steps: the account page's calls to the flag moved from off to split to fully on, and once it was on, the average-per-item calculation divided by this month's purchase count, which is zero for shoppers who bought before but not this month.

I'm checking the spend summary deploy history and the other flag changes before settling on the mechanism, and recording which causes the change events rule out.

I'm making sure the draft pull request is described without quoting its number, and I'm avoiding the exact line number in the log, since the file and the name are enough to point the reader to it.

action_items.item: Roll out feature flag switch-ons in production to a small share of traffic first, and widen them only while the service's error rate stays at its usual level.
Require tests that exercise the code path a feature flag turns on, including shoppers with no purchases in the period it covers, before that flag can be switched on in production.
Decide whether `average_spend_per_item`, used with the flag off, should still raise for an account with no purchases at all, which the current tests expect. If it should not, fix it.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the account page error rate rose far above its usual level.

The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError: division by zero in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, at the line the log names. This error started in the minute the flag was switched on and kept going until the log lines that were read end.

ruled_out.what: A deploy or release. The production change events that were read returned no deploy, only the flag change.
Another flag change. The flag provider's history showed no other flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour before it was read.

causal_chain.step: The account page reached that code because admin switched on the feature flag monthly-spend-feature at {P1.1}. The page's flag evaluations were all off over {G7e5d.4}, split between off and on in {G971b.6}, and all on over {Gce95.4}.

With the flag on, the account page's figure is computed by dividing the month's spend by the number of purchases made this month, and that number is zero for a shopper who has bought before but not this month.

input.cause_in_plain_words: An administrator switched on a new feature for the account page, and it likely sent shoppers who had bought nothing this month through a calculation that divides by their number of purchases this month, which fails when that number is zero.

contributing_factors.factor: When monthly-spend-feature was switched on, it reached the account page's whole traffic within the minute after the change. No staged rollout, or check of the error rate on a small share of traffic, was seen before that.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A staged rollout would have shown the division error on a small share of account page requests and stopped there, so far fewer shoppers would have had failed pages.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No test was seen that exercises the account page with monthly-spend-feature on for a shopper who has no purchases this month. By Code-Fix's reading, the existing tests check only the flag-off path's error.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division error would have been caught before the flag was switched on in production.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent formed candidate C1, which tied the failures to the monthly-spend-feature flag change and the division error in the logs.
The Mitigation Agent reverted monthly-spend-feature from on to off. This needed no deploy and can be put back.
The Mitigation Agent confirmed that the service had left the incident's level after the revert.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request for a person to review.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, the account page's spend summary goes through `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the month's total by the number of purchases marked as this month's, and has no case for a shopper who has bought before but not this month: for that shopper the count is zero and the division raises ZeroDivisionError.
input.still_at_risk: Switching monthly-spend-feature back on before a fix is in place could again fail account pages for shoppers with no purchases this month, and by Code-Fix's reading, the account page can still fail with the flag off for an account with no purchases at all.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for many shoppers
